summary.headline: Grasim Q2 FY27 standalone revenue hit a record Rs 12,747 crore (+33% YoY), but adjusted PAT fell 10% after a Rs 825 crore Birla Jute-type exceptional charge on the Canadian pulp JV.
summary.overview: Grasim reported record consolidated revenue of Rs 50,105 crore and standalone revenue of Rs 12,747 crore (+33% YoY). Standalone reported PAT was hit by an exceptional charge of Rs 825 crore related to idling the Canadian dissolving pulp JV (Rs 767 crore share at the unconsolidated level), with adjusted standalone PAT stated at Rs 3,132 crore. Paints (Birla Opus) grew revenue 35% YoY to Rs 1,337 crore but flat QoQ realisations and competitive scheme intensity weighed on the quarter; management guides H2 paints growth of about 50% YoY. Cellulosic fibres and chemicals drove standalone growth, while chemicals margins were pressured by weak epoxy and specialty demand.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever; TTM Rs 1,94,230 crore, up 11% vs FY26
2.6x YoY, led by dividend income from UltraTech

financial_highlights.metric: Exceptional charge (Canada JV pulp mill idling)
financial_highlights.value: Rs 825 crore standalone; Rs 767 crore at unconsolidated level

financial_highlights.change: +34% YoY; adjusted PAT down 10% YoY (tax on higher dividend income)

segments.name: Paints (Birla Opus)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 1,337 crore (+35% YoY), volume +20% YoY, with realisations roughly flat QoQ despite dealer price list hikes. Management says price gap to the market leader narrowed to 2-4% by September (ex-10% GST effect) from a wider start to the year.

segments.name: Cellulosic fibres (VFY/CSF)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 5,344 crore (+29% YoY) on volume growth, favourable mix and stable domestic realisations. Global CSF prices up four straight quarters; Q2 average USD 1.85/kg (+23% YoY); China operating rates 93%.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 2,759 crore (+15% YoY). CPVC (50,000 t) commissioned Aug 2026 and epichlorohydrin (50,000 t) in Oct 2026; chlorine integration to rise to 67%. Epoxy and specialty margins compressed by weak demand and higher BPA/ECH costs.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 2,785 crore (+66% YoY per management); annualised run-rate above Rs 11,000 crore, target above Rs 12,000 crore for FY27. Management says breakeven is on track for H2 FY27.

segments.name: Aditya Birla Capital (financial services)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 13,990 crore (+32% YoY), broad-based across lending, insurance and asset management.

segments.name: UltraTech (cement)
segments.commentary: Sales volume 38.2 Mt (+~13% YoY), EBITDA +17% YoY. On track for 242.9 Mtpa capacity by end of the fiscal year (as stated).

segments.name: Other businesses (textiles, insulators, renewables)
segments.commentary: Segment revenue +16% YoY, EBITDA +14% YoY. Renewable capacity 2.2 GW peak (+269 MW YoY); target 20 GW; Spring acquisition awaiting CCI approval, closing targeted in calendar 2026.

guidance_outlook: Paints: H2 FY27 revenue growth guided at about 50% YoY; management says October trends were strong; target to reach double-digit revenue market share in H2 FY27.
Paints: target of Rs 10,000 crore brand by exit of FY28 and to become India's second-largest decorative paints company.
Paints: capex of about Rs 10,000 crore in total, with about Rs 3-4 crore-equivalent (3-4 billion rupees) short of plan spent so far, per the call.
Birla Pivot: FY27 revenue target above Rs 12,000 crore; breakeven on track in H2 FY27.
Standalone capex FY27 earmarked at Rs 3,157 crore, of which Rs 1,022 crore spent in H1 FY27.
VSF: Q3 margins expected to be broadly range-bound versus Q2; sulfur prices slightly moderating.
Chemicals: management expects chlorine demand-supply to improve and Q4 epoxy margins to be somewhat better; no major change expected in Q3.
capex_capacity: Cellulosic fibres: specialty fibre expansion of 165,000 tpa in two phases; phase 1 (55,000 tpa) procurement nearly complete; phase 2 (110,000 tpa) environmental clearance application at advanced stage.
Chemicals: 50,000 t CPVC commissioned Aug 2026; 50,000 t epichlorohydrin commissioned Oct 2026. Total capacity about 2.6 Mtpa (1.5 Mt caustic, 1.1 Mt chlorine derivatives).
Power plant: reliability fixes with OEMs; additional boiler being commissioned for redundancy; grid connection added. Management expects no significant volume impact in H2.
Canada JV (pulp mill, Nacoyah-equivalent): board decided to idle operations; Grasim to contribute its 45% share of Rs 625 crore to cover liabilities, with payback expected within about 4 years.
Paints: about 150 depots, 1,760+ exclusive franchise stores (about 300 added in the quarter), 61,000+ retail dealers.
Renewables: 2.2 GW peak capacity; renewable share of power rose to 26% in H1 FY27 from 11% in FY25.
demand_pricing: Paints industry grew about 16-17% in H1 FY27 (about 8-9% price, 7-8% volume); management expects 15-20% industry growth in H2.
Paints: Q2 is seasonally weak (about 42-43% of revenue in H1 vs 57-58% in H2); competitors used heavier schemes to push primary sales into dealers.
Paints: secondary (sell-out) volume to contractors/painters grew 34% YoY vs primary 20%; about 1 million contractors and painters applied Birla Opus products in Q2.
Caustic soda: CFR Southeast Asia at around USD 390/t, a five-year low; domestic chlorine prices improved on local demand.
Epoxy: demand sluggish and BPA/ECH costs rising, squeezing margins; management is trading volume for margin.
VSF: crude-linked raw material costs (sulfur, pulp) rose sharply; difficult to pass through the value chain. Q2 prices held stable.
Global CSF: operating rates 93% in China, inventory 6 days; demand-supply balance described as tight.

qa_highlights.question: Does H2 paints revenue growth need to match H1's 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 50% YoY growth guidance for H2 paints, citing H2 seasonality, strong October throughput and a 15-20% industry growth assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Is paints capex running behind plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall paints capex remains Rs 10,000 crore; about Rs 3-4 billion short of plan spent so far, mainly on franchise setup and printing machines.

qa_highlights.question: Did Birla Opus gain revenue market share in Q2 and how did discounts move?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue market share gain in Q2; discounts were higher industry-wide. Birla Opus narrowed the price gap to 2-4% by September, while its discounts were lower than peers. Management still targets double-digit share in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for VSF margins into Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q3 to be range-bound vs Q2, with crude and polyester costs still elevated and sulfur prices only slightly easing. No firm numerical guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the Rs 625 crore Canada JV provision?
qa_highlights.answer: The pulp mill was loss-making due to reliability, maintenance and cost issues. Grasim holds 45% and will fund its share of wind-down and liabilities over about 4 years; about 20% of Grasim's pulp came from this mill and is now sourced elsewhere.

qa_highlights.question: Chlorine vs caustic pricing and specialty chemical margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Chlorine prices firmed on domestic supply-demand; caustic is under pressure from global supply. Epoxy margins are compressed by weak demand, and management expects a cyclical recovery rather than a structural change.

risks_watch: H2 paints revenue must grow about 50% YoY; the guidance rests on festive-season throughput and a 15-20% industry growth assumption, with no Q2 revenue market share gain and discounts still elevated across the industry.

Crude-linked raw material costs (sulfur, pulp, polyester) remain elevated; VSF Q3 margins guided only as range-bound with no numerical guidance, and pass-through to downstream textile value chain is limited.

Caustic soda under pressure at about USD 390/t CFR Southeast Asia, a five-year low; epoxy margins compressed by sluggish demand and rising BPA/ECH costs; management expects recovery in Q4 but cautioned on geopolitical swings.

Canada pulp JV idling: Rs 625 crore contribution for Grasim's 45% stake, with about 20% of Grasim's pulp previously sourced from the mill now coming from other sources; execution of wind-down and supply substitution to be monitored.
Birla Pivot breakeven targeted in H2 FY27 with FY27 revenue above Rs 12,000 crore; margin and working capital improvement still to be demonstrated.

Paints capex of about Rs 10,000 crore: management says about Rs 3-4 billion short of plan so far; standalone FY27 capex of Rs 3,157 crore with Rs 1,022 crore spent in H1, so H2 spend must rise sharply.
key_quotes: That is the business we are building and we are beginning to see market momentum.
So we expect H2 to be significantly better than H1 and that should help us to reach our business numbers for the third.

Our discounts have been lower and on overall basis the discounts in quarter to one higher side which brings me to the whole commentary of the logical deduction that we've given reasons for high discounting is when you give to certain large dealers for storing larger than inventories and wholesaling that you tend to do larger schemes for for the market which is not the model that we operate.
So it is very cyclical there is no structural change actually in the end industry.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on paints H2 recovery and on the Birla Pivot and renewables growth story, but cautious and evasive on near-term margins, declining to give numerical VSF or chemicals guidance and conceding Q2 revenue market share was not gained. On the Canada JV charge and paints market share, answers were direct on rationale but hedged on specifics such as the market share figure, which was described as a derived number.

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 Birla Opus paints revenue growth of about 50% YoY, backed by 20% Q2 volume growth, 15-20% expected H2 industry growth, a strong October and 1 million contractors applying its products, plus CPVC and epichlorohydrin capacity commissioned in Aug and Oct 2026; no specific paints capacity or order numbers were given for the H2 step-up.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Chemicals margins squeezed (epoxy/specialty, BPA/ECH costs up) and VSF Q3 guided only range-bound with sulfur easing slightly; Q4 epoxy margins guided 'somewhat better', while standalone EBITDA of Rs 4,615 crore was flattered by UltraTech dividend income.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: CPVC 50,000 t commissioned Aug 2026 and epichlorohydrin 50,000 t in Oct 2026 (chlorine integration to 67%), and specialty CSF phase 1 of 55,000 tpa in procurement, with phase 2 of 110,000 tpa awaiting environmental clearance; paints depots and franchise stores also being added (about 300 in Q2).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Paints volume grew 20% YoY in Q2 and H1 volume +33%; management guides H2 paints revenue +50% YoY on 15-20% industry growth, strong October and 1 million contractors applying Birla Opus, though no Q2 share gain was achieved.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Standalone FY27 capex of Rs 3,157 crore has only Rs 1,022 crore spent in H1 and paints capex is Rs 3-4 billion behind plan, so catch-up is likely, but no new capex announcement was made; utilisation not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Birla Pivot revenue of Rs 2,785 crore (+66% YoY) with run-rate above Rs 11,000 crore and FY27 target lifted to above Rs 12,000 crore; paints H2 +50% guided, but no formal upgrade of consolidated guidance was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 paints +50% depends on festive throughput and 15-20% industry growth amid heavy scheme intensity; VSF margins range-bound with elevated crude-linked costs; caustic at USD 390/t, a five-year low; Canada JV idling costs Rs 625 crore for Grasim's 45% stake.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new brands or models announced; the new products are capacity additions (CPVC, epichlorohydrin, specialty CSF) rather than new product launches.

rows.label: Birla Pivot breakeven in H2 FY27
rows.why: Management says breakeven is on track for H2 FY27 with FY27 revenue target above Rs 12,000 crore against a run-rate above Rs 11,000 crore.

rows.label: Canada JV pulp mill idling
rows.why: Board has decided to idle the mill; Grasim's 45% share of Rs 625 crore to be paid over about 4 years, with about 20% of Grasim's pulp now sourced elsewhere.

rows.label: Spring acquisition closing
rows.why: Spring acquisition awaiting CCI approval with closing targeted in calendar 2026; renewables at 2.2 GW peak and target 20 GW.

tone.note: Management was confident on the paints H2 recovery (50% growth guided), Birla Pivot breakeven and renewables, but cautious on near-term chemicals and VSF margins and conceded no Q2 paints revenue share gain; analysts pushed on the paints market share and discount intensity, and the Canada JV rationa
